Alex.confusing: How a Wink and the Hugged/Confused effects interact with reports; also unclear whether the Eagle's visitor list includes Meowfia-only visits like the Floofer.
Alex.fun: Round 3, calling out the duplicate Tit claim and getting the table to eggsecute Finley, the Floofer, in one coordinated throw.
Alex.change: Announce the number of Meowfia each round, or give Meowfia a way to learn each other, because they are blind and easy to eliminate.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Hawk on Drew when I had actually visited Casey, and Casey's Falcon report exposed the lie. I should have claimed a vaguer role, or kept the Wink to use on someone.

Blair.confusing: How eggsecution scoring works when my side loses: only the highest card returns, and the rest of the throw is discarded. That made big throws on a losing team costly. I also couldn't tell how confusion and hugging interact with the reports.
Blair.fun: Round 1, when I caught Alex's false Hawk claim. My Owl result (only a Falcon visited Drew) contradicted him, and the table piled onto him quickly.
Blair.change: Let Meowfia learn at least one teammate's identity, or give them a way to coordinate. Playing alone as Meowfia with a single Wink felt weak, and I couldn't coordinate any play with Finley.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I claimed Tit, which Alex really was. It made me look like a liar and pulled suspicion onto me. I should have claimed a vaguer role, or Pigeon, and pushed Finley with the rest of the table. I also never used my Wink.

Casey.confusing: Why Meowfia don't know each other yet can still be teamed up, and how the Floofer's hug interacts with visitor reports. In round 2 it was hard to tell why nothing registered on Ellis.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when I used my Eagle info to confirm Drew's and Ellis's stories and the table converged on Finley. Throwing four high cards and banking 27 points felt good.
Casey.change: Add a way for the Meowfia to coordinate or at least know whether they have a partner. Playing a lone Meowfia with only a Wink felt weak.
Casey.regret: In round 2 as Mouser I bluffed Falcon with a muddled story and wasted my turn. I should have claimed something clean, like a Pigeon who visited someone unverifiable. Or I could have used the Wink on a key accuser, since I threw at Ellis and lost anyway.

Drew.confusing: Why my Owl report in round 2 showed nothing when others claimed to visit Ellis, and how Floofer hugs interact with Owl reports. It was unclear whether a hugged or empty report looks different.
Drew.fun: Round 1, when the table converged on Alex after the contradicting visitor claims, and the Eagle and Owl cross-checks caught him lying.
Drew.change: Give the leader less of a runaway advantage, or make the standings clearer during the game. Ellis banked big early and it was hard to catch up when every round went to Farm.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I kept H4 and threw only 3 cards at Ellis, though I was fairly confident. I should have thrown all 4 to bank more points. I also didn't use my Kookaburra visit in round 3 to target someone suspicious, and picked the leader instead.

Ellis.confusing: Mostly nothing. How Kookaburra confusion and hugs interact with dawn reports was a bit unclear, and so was what the "+0" nest changes could reveal.
Ellis.fun: Round 3, when my Owl report showed only a Floofer visited Drew. That exposed Finley's Pigeon lie and let the table converge fast.
Ellis.change: Give Meowfia some way to coordinate or find each other. As it is, they mostly bluff alone, and the leader gets piled on.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 as Floofer I claimed Hawk, the same role Finley claimed. That guaranteed a conflict and got me eggsecuted. I'd claim an unclaimed role, or a Pigeon, and throw with the majority to avoid standing out.

Finley.confusing: Nothing major, though how hugs and confusion interact with other roles' reports (like Drew's Kookaburra being confused by my Floofer visit) wasn't obvious until the day discussion.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I was Farm and the table converged on Ellis, the other Hawk claimant. It was Meowfia and I banked 32 points from three cards.
Finley.change: I'd make the Floofer's hug leave some trace, or give Meowfia a way to learn who their partner is. As it was, a lone Floofer had little to work with and no safe cover story.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I claimed Pigeon after hugging Drew. Drew had lost eggs, and a Pigeon lays eggs, so the claim didn't fit, and Ellis's Owl report exposed it. I should have claimed a role with no egg effect, like Hawk or Falcon, or said I visited someone else.

review.title: Everyone Visits the Leader
review.headline: Three rounds of piling on the obvious suspect, and the leader still won.
review.summary: Each round the table settled on one target fast and was right every time. Alex was caught lying about his visit in round 1. Ellis was the leader and had a duplicate Hawk claim in round 2. Finley's Pigeon claim was contradicted by Ellis's Owl report in round 3. Ellis banked big throws in rounds 1 and 3 and finished first with 65. The Meowfia never had a real chance to win a round.

rounds.recap: Alex (Mouser) claimed Hawk on Drew but had actually visited Casey. Ellis's Eagle report exposed this. Finley (Floofer) first claimed Pigeon, then switched to Kookaburra when caught. The table still piled on Alex. Ellis threw six cards and banked 45 points.

Ellis (Floofer) hugged Drew. Everyone else visited Ellis, and every visit was blocked or showed nothing. Ellis and Finley both claimed Hawk. The table went for the leader Ellis, who was Meowfia. Casey, the other Meowfia, hid with a muddled Falcon claim and threw with the crowd, so the Meowfia team lost.

Finley (Floofer) hugged Drew and claimed Pigeon. Ellis's Owl saw only a Floofer visit Drew, which exposed him. Casey's Eagle list backed Ellis's story. Blair (Mouser) copied a Tit claim and threw at Alex, but Finley was eggsecuted anyway. Blair never used his Wink.

highlights.text: Ellis's Eagle list of Alex, Drew and Finley visiting Casey caught Alex in his Hawk lie, and also caught Finley's fake Pigeon claim.
Five players visited Ellis and nothing registered. That left a pile of claims that could not be checked.
Ellis's Owl report that only a Floofer visited Drew was a clean, checkable fact. It broke Finley's Pigeon lie, and Casey's Eagle list backed it.
Blair, the Mouser, threw his 13 at a Farm player so it would return. This was a smart hedge after his team was clearly losing.

confusions.what: Claimed Falcon and then muddled the result mid-sentence ('they visited nobody... no wait'). Seems unsure how Falcon reports work.
Claimed Owl and said his empty report was odd. He did not realize he was hugged, or that an Owl hears only animals that visited.

Said three players claimed to visit Ellis and none did, implying three liars. He missed that the hug on Ellis or the hugs on the visitors could explain it. Ellis's Floofer hug was on Drew, but Ellis was not hugged himself.
Said Alex's Eagle would have gotten an egg from Blair's visit. Eagles gain an egg per visitor, but Blair visited Ellis, not Alex. He misread who visited whom.

Said a Pigeon lays eggs so Finley's claim does not fit his -2. A Pigeon visit would add eggs, but Drew was confused, so the report was unreliable. He was reasoning from a report he had been told to doubt.
Gave a garbled line about who visited both Ellis and Drew. It was confusing and did not help.

worked: Eagle and Owl visitor reports gave checkable facts. In rounds 1 and 3 they broke lies cleanly and made the table feel clever.
Consolation return of the highest card when throwing at the other team. Alex, Blair and Finley used it to hedge when losing.
Public nest-size changes. The +3 for Ellis (R1) and Casey (R3) gave everyone a clue to cross-check against claims.
Throw counts as a signal. Ellis's six-card throw and the small Finley throws gave readable confidence cues.
problems: Meowfia lose almost always. Cats don't know each other, have weak info roles, and the table converges on one target within a beat or two. Fix: give cats a way to sow doubt or coordinate, or a Wink that is easier to use.

Mouser's Wink was never used in rounds 1 to 3. Alex and Blair held it and Casey held it in round 2. Probably the day is too short, or killing a speaker is not attractive. Consider making it stronger or time-sensitive.
Floofer hugs block everything and produce silent nights. In round 2 five visits to Ellis registered nothing, and the table had no way to reason about it. Fix: tell hugged players they were hugged.
Early CAW CAW ended every day after beat 2 of 4. Players called it as soon as a consensus formed, which cut discussion short and killed second thoughts. Raise the CAW threshold or delay it.

The leader snowballs. Ellis banked 45 points in round 1 with a six-card throw, then won the game. Winning rounds by consensus pays out hugely for whoever holds big nests. Consider capping banked cards per throw or scaling points.
